originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons cover rotating-camera placement precision, published fixed-budget Poisson detection with fitted gamma/lognormal rates, general deadline restart principles, and mixed-rate animal foraging. The published inspected conclusions do not directly state or logically imply without further argument the all-distribution threshold c=-log(q)/lambda0, the positive-atom equality boundary or every ordered consecutive integer phase. Semantic mathematical record searches over alternative formulations, lowest-rate atoms and fixed-cost rotations found nearby but different claims. This is a provisional same-model originality assessment, not a proof of total historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: General restart, foraging, or resource-allocation literature outside the material inspected may imply the atomic criterion, despite the specific distinctions documented.

The 1991 Poisson-patch article was available as a web text extract but some displayed equations were garbled; the optimization objective differs, and a full-typographic comparison remains a historical-priority uncertainty.
Gamma and lognormal special-case optimizers are prior art; neither those cases nor the generic concavity/Jensen reduction are claimed as independent original results.

value.rationale: The exact all-budget no-relocation criterion is decided by the essential minimum encounter rate and its point mass, not merely rate mean/variance, and produces an atom/no-atom phase reversal with real operational meaning for independent-site wildlife survey planning. The result also completely orders integer survey counts and gives an exact efficient two-neighbor optimizer for arbitrary known rate mixtures. It is structurally different from published gamma-only survey optimizers and from data-estimation precision studies; empirical calibration and independence assumptions explicitly limit applications.
